questions.question:
The following bar graph shows the number of males, number of females and total population of four different villages. Find the total number of children in the four villages.

Total population = Number of Males + Number of Females + Number of Children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aef9ed6a4c0600c5ef100cce63be9c93b3ca5132bfa539fe96e4a795b86d0156.png]
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Children in A = 1500 - (820 + 400) = 280

Children in B = 1600 - (1040 + 320) = 240

Children in C = 1400 - (760 + 420) = 220

Children in D = 1000 - (580 + 300) = 120

Total number of children in all the villages = 280 + 240 + 220 + 120 = 860

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: X and Y together can do a piece of work in 30 days. Z alone can do it in 60 days. If they worked together, then in how many days they can finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

X and Y can do a work in 30 days, Z can do it alone in 60 days.

Formula:

(1/(X+Y)) + (1/Z) = 1/Total

Calculation:

⇒ (1/30) + (1/60) = 1/Total

⇒ Total = 20 days.

Hence, they can finish the work in 20 days.

questions.question: A person sold an article at a loss of 4%. Had he sold it at a gain of 1%, he would have received Rs. 42.5 more. To gain 18%, what must be his selling price?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Loss of 4% = Cost Price - Selling Price, Gain of 1% = Selling Price - Cost Price

**Calculation:**

⇒ 5% = 42.5

⇒ Cost Price = 42.5 × (100/5) = 850

⇒ Selling Price for 18% gain = 850 + 18% of 850 = Rs. 1003

**Therefore, to gain 18%, the selling price should be Rs. 1003.**

questions.solution:

[0.004 × {5 ÷ (21 - 6) × 3} + 0.8]

BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Calculations:**

[0.004 × {5 ÷ 15 × 3} + 0.8]

⇒ [0.004 × {(5)/(15) × 3} + 0.8]

questions.question: Find the difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years on a sum of Rs. 11000 at a rate of 11% per annum.
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Principal = Rs. 11000, Rate = 11%, Time = 2 years

**Formula:**

CI - SI = PR²/(100)²

**Calculation:**

⇒ CI - SI = 11000 × 11²/(100)2

⇒Rs. 133.1

**Therefore, the difference between compound interest and simple interest is Rs. 133.1.**

questions.question: If 750 is divided into two parts such that the ratio of one to the other is in the ratio 8 ∶ 7, then find the smallest number.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total number = 750, Ratio = 8 : 7

**Calculation:**

⇒ Smallest number = 750 × (7/15) = 350

**Hence, the smallest number is 350.**

questions.question: Successive discount of 15% and 35% is equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Successive discounts of 15% and 35%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Equivalent discount = 1 - (1 - 15/100) × (1 - 35/100) = 0.4475 or 44.75%

**Therefore, successive discounts of 15% and 35% is equivalent to a single discount of 0.4475 or 44.75%.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 11500 amounts to Rs. 12880 in 2 years at the rate of simple interest. What is the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 11500, Amount after 2 years = Rs. 12880

**Formula:**

Rate = 100 × (SI/PT)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Rate = 100 × ((12880 - 11500)/(11500 × 2)) = 6% per annum

**Hence, the rate of interest is 6% per annum.**

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 44 km/hr and the speed of a stream is 26 km/hr. Find the upstream speed of boat.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of boat = 44 km/hr, Speed of stream = 26 km/hr

**Formula:**

Upstream speed = Speed of boat - Speed of stream

**Calculation:**

⇒ Upstream speed = 44 - 26 = 18 km/hr

**Therefore, the upstream speed of the boat is 18 km/hr.**

questions.question: The price of sugar is increased by 40%. By what percentage must one cut down on the consumption of sugar so that no extra amount has to be incurred on sugar?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the fractional reduction rule for constant expenditure:

Price increase = 40% = 2/5

If price increases by a fraction a/b, consumption must decrease by a/(a+b) to keep expenditure constant.

Required consumption reduction = 2 / (2 + 5) = 2/7

Percentage reduction = (2 ÷ 7) × 100 = 28.57% ≈ 28.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 28.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in the price of sugar = 40%

**Concept Used:**

When Expenditure remains constant, Price and Consumption are inversely proportional (Expenditure = Price × Consumption).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e1e2dc75ad8d79ab530897b421bac313d7e946174f1eec10b033b01453d8b55.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price of sugar be ₹100 per unit and initial consumption be 100 units.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 100 = ₹10000

⇒ New price of sugar after 40% increase = ₹140 per unit

⇒ To keep the expenditure constant at ₹10000, New Consumption = 10000 ÷ 140 = 500 / 7 units

⇒ Reduction in consumption = Original Consumption − New Consumption

⇒ Reduction in consumption = 100 − (500 / 7) = (700 − 500) / 7 = 200 / 7 units

⇒ Percentage reduction = [(Reduction in consumption) ÷ (Original Consumption)] × 100

⇒ Percentage reduction = [(200 / 7) ÷ 100] × 100

⇒ Percentage reduction = 200 / 7 % = 28.57%

⇒ Looking at the options, it is approximately 28.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 28.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price & Consumption Rule (Increase)

If the price of a commodity increases by R%, the required percentage reduction in consumption so as not to increase the overall expenditure is given by [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%.

Price & Consumption Rule (Decrease)

If the price of a commodity decreases by R%, the permissible percentage increase in consumption to maintain the exact same expenditure is given by [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100%.

Constant Product Rule

For any equation of the form A × B = Constant, if variable A increases by a fraction of x/y, then variable B must decrease by the fraction x/(x+y) to keep their product constant.

questions.question: P alone can complete a work in 15 days and Q alone can complete the same work in 12 days. They start the work together but after 3 days P leaves the work. How much time will Q take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(15, 12) = 60 units.

Efficiency of P = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units/day | Efficiency of Q = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units/day.

Work done together in 3 days = 3 × (4 + 5) = 27 units.

Remaining time for Q = (60 − 27) ÷ 5 = 33 ÷ 5 = 6.6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 15 days.

Time taken by Q to complete the work = 12 days.

P and Q work together for 3 days, then P leaves.

**Method Used:**

LCM Method: Total Work = LCM of individual days.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P
 15
 60
 4
 
 

 Q
 12
 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = 60 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P and Q = 4 + 5 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by P and Q in 3 days = 9 × 3 = 27 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 27 = 33 units.

⇒ Time taken by Q to finish the remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Q's efficiency.

⇒ Time taken by Q = 33 ÷ 5 = 6.6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fractional Work Method

If a person completes a job in x days, then the part of the work completed in 1 day is 1/x. Work remaining after n days is 1 − (n ÷ x).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by the individuals. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept of time and work directly applies to pipes and cisterns. Filling a tank is considered positive work, while emptying a tank is considered negative work.

questions.question: The length of two parallel sides of a trapezium are 15 metre and 20 metre. If its height is 22 metre, then what is the area of the trapezium?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Lengths of parallel sides = 15m and 20m, Height = 22m

**Formula:**

Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (sum of lengths of parallel sides) × height

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (15 + 20) × 22 = 385 metre2

**Hence, the area of the trapezium is 385 metre2**

questions.question: In a match, average runs scored by 4 batsmen is 48 . If the runs scored by three batsmen are 58,28 and 24 respectively, then how many runs did the fourth player score?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average runs of 4 batsmen = 48, Runs scored by three batsmen = 58, 28, 24

**Calculation:**

⇒ Runs scored by fourth player = (4 × 48) - (58 + 28 + 24) = 82

**Hence, the fourth player scored 82 runs.**

questions.question: If A ∶ B is 7 ∶ 4 and A - B = 9, then what is the value of A + B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A ∶ B = 7 ∶ 4, A - B = 9

**Calculation:**

⇒ A = 9 × 7/(7 - 4) = 21

⇒ B = 9 × 4/(7 - 4) = 12

⇒ A + B = 21 + 12 = 33

**Therefore, the value of A + B is 33.**

questions.question: The average age of six brothers is 15 years. If their father is also included, the average is increased by 7 years. Find the age of the father (in years).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average age of six brothers = 15, Average age when father included = 22

**Calculation:**

⇒ Father's age = 22 × 7 - 15 × 6 = 64 years

**Hence, the age of the father is 64 years.**

questions.question: Three metal rods of length 77 cm, 110 cm and 121 cm are to be cut into parts of equal length. Each part must be as long as possible. What is the maximum number of pieces that can be cut?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To get pieces as long as possible, length of each piece must be HCF(77, 110, 121).

HCF(77, 110, 121) = 11 cm.

Total pieces = (Length 1 ÷ HCF) + (Length 2 ÷ HCF) + (Length 3 ÷ HCF)

Total pieces = (77 ÷ 11) + (110 ÷ 11) + (121 ÷ 11)

Total pieces = 7 + 10 + 11 = 28.

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lengths of metal rods = 77 cm, 110 cm, 121 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Maximum length of each part = HCF of rod lengths.

Total number of pieces = (Total length of all rods) ÷ (Length of one part).

 
 77 cm (7 × 11 cm)
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 110 cm (10 × 11 cm)
 
• 
 
 
 121 cm (11 × 11 cm)
 
• 

 Each segment length = HCF(77, 110, 121) = 11 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors of 77 = 7 × 11

⇒ Prime factors of 110 = 2 × 5 × 11

⇒ Prime factors of 121 = 11 × 11

⇒ HCF (77, 110, 121) = 11 cm

⇒ Max length of each part = 11 cm

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 1 = 77 ÷ 11 = 7

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 2 = 110 ÷ 11 = 10

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 3 = 121 ÷ 11 = 11

⇒ Total maximum pieces = 7 + 10 + 11 = 28

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

It is the greatest number that divides each of the given numbers exactly without leaving any remainder.

Cutting Problems

When objects of different lengths are cut into equal pieces of maximum possible length, that length is always the HCF of the original lengths.

Number of Pieces Formula

Total Pieces = (Σ Lengths) ÷ HCF. Here, (77 + 110 + 121) ÷ 11 = 308 ÷ 11 = 28.</p

questions.question: A man buys 21 mangoes for a rupee. How many mangoes had he sold for a rupee so that there is a loss of 30 percent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Buying price = 21 mangoes for a rupee,

Loss = 30%

**Calculation:**

For 30% loss, he has to sell all 21 mangoes in 70% of 1Rs.

Thus, SP of 21 Mangoes = 0.7 Rs

So in 1 Rs he has to sell =21/0.7 mangoes = 30 mangoes

**Hence, he had to sell around 30 mangoes for a rupee to have a loss of 30%.**
